question: What is a Letter of Undertaking (LUT) in the context of GST?
reference_answer: An LUT is a self-declaration furnished by a registered exporter on the GST portal (Form GST RFD-11) allowing them to export goods or services, or supply to SEZs, without paying IGST, in place of executing a bond.

question: Which form is used to furnish a Letter of Undertaking?
reference_answer: Form GST RFD-11 is used to furnish the Letter of Undertaking on the GST common portal.

question: When is an LUT deemed to be accepted?
reference_answer: An LUT is deemed accepted as soon as an acknowledgement bearing the Application Reference Number (ARN) is generated online, with no further approval needed from a tax officer.

question: Who is not eligible to furnish an LUT?
reference_answer: A person who has been prosecuted for tax evasion involving an amount of Rs 2.5 crore or more under the CGST Act, IGST Act, or existing law is not eligible to furnish an LUT and must instead execute a bond.

question: Under Section 2(6) of the IGST Act, what conditions must be met for a supply of service to qualify as an export?
reference_answer: Under Section 2(6) of the IGST Act, a supply of service qualifies as export if the supplier is located in India, the recipient is located outside India, the place of supply is outside India, payment is received in convertible foreign exchange (or Indian Rupees where permitted by RBI), and the supplier and recipient are not merely establishments of a distinct person.

question: How does the IGST Act define an intermediary under Section 2(13)?
reference_answer: Section 2(13) defines an intermediary as a broker, agent, or any other person who arranges or facilitates the supply of goods, services, or securities between two or more persons, but does not include a person who supplies such goods or services on their own account.

question: What does Section 13 of the IGST Act cover?
reference_answer: Section 13 of the IGST Act determines the place of supply of services where the location of the supplier or the location of the recipient is outside India.

question: I am a freelance developer in India providing software services to a client based in Germany. Do I qualify as exporting services under GST?
reference_answer: Yes, provided you are located in India, the German client is located outside India, the place of supply is outside India, payment is received in convertible foreign exchange, and you and the client are not establishments of the same distinct person, this qualifies as an export of services under Section 2(6) of the IGST Act.

question: If I subcontract part of a client project to another freelancer, does that make me an intermediary under GST?
reference_answer: No. If you are supplying the main service to the client on your own account, even if you subcontract part of the execution, you are not an intermediary. An intermediary is someone who merely arranges or facilitates a supply between two other parties without supplying the main service themselves.

question: Does an IT-enabled/BPO service provider handling customer support for a foreign company qualify as an export of services or as an intermediary?
reference_answer: Per CBIC clarification (Circular 107/26/2019-GST), providers of back-office/IT-enabled support services who supply the service on their own account to the foreign company qualify as exporters, not intermediaries, provided they are not merely arranging or facilitating a supply between the foreign company and its own customers.

question: Does a data hosting service provider qualify as an intermediary under GST?
reference_answer: Per CBIC clarification, a data hosting service provider generally supplies the hosting service on its own account directly to the recipient and does not arrange or facilitate a supply between two other parties, so it does not qualify as an intermediary.

question: If I miss the deadline to file my LUT for a financial year, can I still export without paying IGST?
reference_answer: An LUT must be furnished prior to export. If it has not been filed, the exporter is generally required to pay IGST on the export and can later claim a refund, or must execute a bond instead of an LUT, until a valid LUT is furnished for the relevant period.

question: What is the process to file an LUT on the GST portal?
reference_answer: Log in to the GST portal, navigate to Services > User Services > Furnish Letter of Undertaking (LUT), select the financial year, fill in the GSTIN, witness details, and self-declarations, and submit. An ARN is generated upon successful submission, after which the LUT is deemed accepted.

question: Can I upload a manually approved LUT instead of filing online?
reference_answer: Yes, if you already have an LUT that was approved manually for the relevant financial year, you can upload that document as part of an online application to bring your records up to date on the portal.

question: What details are required as part of the LUT self-declaration in Form RFD-11?
reference_answer: Form RFD-11 requires the taxpayer's GSTIN, the relevant financial year, details of two witnesses, and self-declarations confirming compliance with the conditions for zero-rated export supply without payment of IGST.

question: What is the exact amount of GST I owe on a ₹5 lakh invoice to a client in Singapore?
reference_answer: This depends on whether the supply meets all conditions to qualify as an export of services (recipient location, place of supply, payment in convertible foreign exchange, LUT filed or bond executed). If all conditions are met, the supply is zero-rated with no GST payable; if not, standard GST applies. A qualified tax professional should confirm the specific liability.

question: What is the current GST registration threshold for service providers in India?
reference_answer: This is subject to change via government notification and should be verified against the latest official notification or a tax professional, rather than relied upon from a static document snapshot.

question: Has any new GST circular been issued this month regarding export of services?
reference_answer: This cannot be answered from a static, previously-indexed document set; the official CBIC website should be checked for the most recent circulars.

question: Should I file GST returns even if all my supplies are zero-rated exports?
reference_answer: Yes, zero-rated exports must still be reported in GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B even though no tax is payable, in order to remain compliant and to support any input tax credit claims.

question: LUT file karna zaroori hai kya agar main foreign client ko service deta hoon?
reference_answer: Haan, agar aap ek registered exporter hain aur bina IGST pay kiye export karna chahte hain, to LUT file karna zaroori hai. Agar LUT file nahi karte, to IGST pay karke baad me refund claim karna padega.

question: Kya main intermediary hoon agar main sirf apni khud ki service deta hoon kisi US client ko directly?
reference_answer: Nahi, agar aap apni service directly apne account par supply kar rahe hain, to aap intermediary nahi hain. Intermediary wo hota hai jo sirf do parties ke beech supply arrange ya facilitate karta hai, khud supply nahi karta.

question: RFD-11 form kya hota hai aur kaise file karte hain?
reference_answer: FORM GST RFD-11 LUT furnish karne ke liye use hota hai. Ise GST portal par Services > User Services > Furnish Letter of Undertaking section me online file kiya jata hai.

question: My marketing agency finds international clients for Indian freelancers and charges them a commission. Is the agency an intermediary?
reference_answer: Yes, an agency that arranges or facilitates a supply between two other parties (the freelancer and the international client) in exchange for a commission, without supplying the main service itself, fits the definition of an intermediary under Section 2(13) of the IGST Act.

question: I directly invoice my overseas client for consulting work, but use a payment gateway to receive funds. Does using a payment gateway make me an intermediary?
reference_answer: No. Using a payment gateway to receive payment does not affect your classification. As long as you are supplying the consulting service directly on your own account, you remain the exporter of services, not an intermediary.

question: A company in India resells software licenses purchased from a foreign vendor to Indian customers under its own name. Is this an export of services?
reference_answer: No, this is not an export of services from India; the company is a domestic reseller supplying to Indian customers, which does not meet the export of services conditions under Section 2(6) of the IGST Act.

question: What happens if an exporter fails to realize export proceeds within the time period allowed under FEMA?
reference_answer: If export proceeds are not realized within the time period allowed under FEMA, the exporter may be liable to pay GST on the supply along with interest, since the export condition of receiving payment in convertible foreign exchange has not been fulfilled within the prescribed timeline.

question: Is a bond with bank guarantee required for all exporters who cannot furnish an LUT?
reference_answer: Exporters who are not eligible to furnish an LUT (such as those prosecuted for tax evasion above the specified threshold) are required to execute a bond, which may need to be backed by a bank guarantee as determined by the jurisdictional officer.

question: Does the place of supply rule under Section 13 apply if both the supplier and recipient are located in India?
reference_answer: No, Section 13 of the IGST Act applies specifically where the location of the supplier or the location of the recipient is outside India; if both parties are located in India, the place of supply is instead determined under Section 12.

question: What is the difference between zero-rated supply and exempt supply under GST?
reference_answer: A zero-rated supply (such as an export) is taxed at 0% and allows the supplier to claim input tax credit on inputs used, whereas an exempt supply is not taxed at all and generally does not allow input tax credit on related inputs.

question: If I supply services to a foreign client but the place of supply is determined to be in India, is it still an export?
reference_answer: No. For a supply to qualify as an export of services, the place of supply must be outside India as per Section 2(6) of the IGST Act; if the place of supply is India, the transaction does not meet the export criteria even if the recipient is located abroad.

question: Can a freelancer file LUT for a financial year that has already ended?
reference_answer: An LUT is meant to be furnished prior to making export supplies for a given financial year; it should be filed at the start of or before undertaking exports for that year, not retroactively after the year has ended.

question: What documents should an exporter maintain to support a zero-rated export claim?
reference_answer: An exporter should maintain the LUT or bond, tax invoices marked for export, proof of receipt of payment in convertible foreign exchange, and relevant shipping or service delivery documentation to support a zero-rated export claim.

question: Does GST apply to advances received for services to be exported?
reference_answer: Advances received for services that will ultimately qualify as export of services under a valid LUT are generally not subject to GST, provided the export conditions are eventually satisfied and properly documented.

question: Is a website/app development agency in India that builds a product for a US startup, receiving equity instead of cash, eligible for export benefits?
reference_answer: This is a genuinely ambiguous scenario since payment in equity rather than convertible foreign exchange may not satisfy the standard export-of-services payment condition; this should be confirmed with a tax professional rather than assumed either way.

question: What is the penalty for not filing GST returns for a zero-rated export supply?
reference_answer: This depends on current late fee and penalty provisions which are subject to periodic revision; the exact amount should be verified against the current CGST Act/Rules or a tax professional rather than assumed from a static source.

question: Can an LUT be furnished for multiple financial years at once?
reference_answer: No, an LUT must be furnished separately for each financial year in which the taxpayer intends to make zero-rated exports without payment of IGST.

question: If my LUT application is rejected, what are my options?
reference_answer: If an LUT application is rejected, the exporter would generally need to either address the reason for rejection and reapply, or execute a bond (potentially with a bank guarantee) to continue exporting without payment of IGST.

question: What is the significance of the ARN generated after LUT submission?
reference_answer: The ARN serves as proof of submission and acknowledgement of the LUT; once generated, the LUT is deemed accepted without requiring further manual approval.

question: A UK-based company has an Indian subsidiary. If the Indian subsidiary provides services to its UK parent, is this treated as an export?
reference_answer: This may not qualify as an export of services if the Indian subsidiary and its UK parent are treated as establishments of a distinct person under the IGST Act, since the export definition excludes supplies between such establishments.

question: Does an exporter need to be GST-registered to file an LUT?
reference_answer: Yes, only a GST-registered person can furnish an LUT; unregistered persons are not eligible to use the LUT mechanism.

question: What should I do if the GST portal doesn't generate an ARN after I submit my LUT?
reference_answer: If the ARN is not generated due to a technical issue, the exporter should retry submission or raise a grievance through the GST portal's support channels; without a valid ARN, the LUT may not be considered furnished.

question: I run a dropshipping business selling physical goods to US customers, invoicing them directly. Does GST export-of-services apply to me?
reference_answer: No, this scenario involves export of goods, not services, which is governed by separate export-of-goods provisions under GST and customs law rather than the export-of-services rules under Section 2(6) of the IGST Act.

question: Can a sole proprietor freelancer furnish an LUT, or is it only for companies?
reference_answer: A sole proprietor freelancer can furnish an LUT as long as they are a GST-registered person meeting the eligibility conditions; the LUT mechanism is not limited to companies.

question: What is Rule 96A of the CGST Rules about?
reference_answer: Rule 96A of the CGST Rules lays down the procedure and conditions for export of goods or services under a Letter of Undertaking or bond, without payment of integrated tax.

question: If I provide consulting services to a client with offices in both India and the US, how is the place of supply determined?
reference_answer: Where the recipient has establishments in more than one location, the place of supply rules generally look to the location most directly concerned with the supply; this can be fact-specific and may need professional confirmation for a given case.

question: Kya intermediary services par bhi GST lagta hai?
reference_answer: Haan, intermediary services generally taxable hoti hain, kyunki intermediary khud koi export nahi kar raha hota, balki sirf commission/facilitation service de raha hota hai jo standard GST rules ke under aata hai.

question: Agar main LUT ke bina export karta hoon to kya IGST refund le sakta hoon baad mein?
reference_answer: Haan, agar LUT file kiye bina IGST pay karke export kiya jata hai, to exporter baad me us IGST ka refund claim kar sakta hai, lekin isme extra compliance aur processing time lagta hai.

question: What counts as 'establishments of a distinct person' under the IGST Act?
reference_answer: Establishments of a distinct person generally refers to different locations or branches of the same legal entity (e.g., a head office and its own branch abroad), and supplies between such establishments are excluded from the definition of export of services.

question: Can GST paid in error on an export supply be adjusted against future liability instead of claiming a refund?
reference_answer: This is a procedural/compliance question with conditions that vary by case; it is best confirmed with a tax professional or through the official refund provisions rather than assumed.

question: Does the LUT need to be renewed every year, and is there a grace period if I miss the renewal?
reference_answer: An LUT is valid only for the financial year for which it is furnished, and a fresh LUT must be filed for each subsequent financial year; specific grace period provisions, if any, should be confirmed against current rules or a professional.
